title: Distributing Dreams
paragraphs: Father and the others stared at Éclair with a somewhat melancholic look.
So, there’s something like dungeon insurance, is there?
“Is that really a dungeon?”
“This is where Gaelion distributes dreams, nano!”
Rival, who had been flying alongside us, suddenly interjected. On his back were the assistant and the mole.
“There are dragons who take pride in expanding their nests, nano! Naturally, they scatter treasures around their nests to prevent them from being taken, nano!”
“Oh! Really?”
“Nano! Plus, as a byproduct, treasures sometimes increase, so dragons welcome adventurers, nano!”
“Byproduct?”
“Adventurers tend to carry a lot of treasures, nano. So, if they die, it all becomes the dragon’s, nano!”
“Ah… I see. You mean the items that adventurers carry.”
“It’s their lifeline, after all. They invest in better equipment, which ends up making them valuable treasures. It makes sense.”
“Nano! Probably, at the lowest level of a big dungeon, there’s a Dragon Emperor, nano. If Gaelion wants to power up even more, defeating it is an option, nano!”
Father and the others perked up at Rival’s words.
“I see… If it’s a dungeon managed by a dragon, then the treasures regenerating makes sense.”
“That’s right, nano!”
Éclair chimed in as well.
Rival getting all the attention is not amusing at all!
“So, the living dungeons where treasures regenerate, which I’ve heard of before, are maintained by someone, is that it?”
“The problem is that if the boss dragon is defeated, the treasure regeneration might stop.”
“The treasure itself might still be obtainable… but then again, adventurers are the ones losing their lives…”
“Either way, it seems that some of the famous dungeons in this country might have been created by dragons.”
“Greed swirls around them, huh? There’s more excitement in that than just treasure hunting in ordinary ruins.”
“Shall we go if we have the time?”
“Yeah, but… we need to be careful not to treat this too much like a game. We’re not fighting for fun.”
Father’s words made Ren and Itsuki nod firmly.
“…Yeah. Even when fighting monsters, I’ve learned that you have to be prepared. If you cut, it bleeds, and if you kill, they don’t come back…”
“That’s right. The people of this world are living beings. They’re not NPCs.”
Back in the first world, when I was chasing pigs, I had similar thoughts. I understand how they feel.
“That’s… yeah. I painfully learned that lesson on the second day of adventuring.”
“Ugh… Yeah, that was a wake-up call from the dream.”
“Please don’t remind me. Yeah, that was definitely the biggest reason!”
Father and the others nodded to each other in agreement. I nodded along with them. For some reason, I got some side-eye.
“Did something happen?”
The second day… that was the glorious day when I took down that crimson swine and trash who tried to trap Father.
“Motoyasu-san, are you really the one to say that…?”
“What’s the point of the culprit saying that…? I had nightmares because of you for a while, I say.”
“Well, I mean, you did save us, but… I can’t really complain because that incident woke me up from the dream instantly. It made me understand what fighting really is…”
“I can only imagine what kind of feelings the heroes went through, but I sympathize.”
Éclair responded quietly.
“Huh?”

Rival and the others tilted their heads, unable to grasp Father’s feelings. Father seemed to consider whether to explain but ultimately decided not to. And so, we continued our journey through the country where the projectile weapon hero was sighted. For now, visiting the adventurer’s guild as a base for gathering information had become the standard procedure. Thanks to the pig king of Faubrey’s signature and the hero’s privileges, we could even obtain classified information.
“Have you found anything?”
“Hmm… It’s mostly just rumors. Even the descriptions are vague.”

We were in a private room, reviewing the testimonies collected by the adventurer’s guild. Well, since Father and the others were still learning to read, there was a limit to how much they could decipher.
“What kind of person are we even looking for?”
Father asked someone who might know the face of the projectile weapon hero.
Indeed. That was precisely this person’s role.
“Well… he gives off a similar vibe to the Sword Hero-sama.”
“Like Ren, huh…”
Father glanced at Ren.
“W-What?”
Ren looked flustered as Father’s gaze settled on him.
“First impression-wise… cool-headed—”
“Kind of a loner who loves solitude but is secretly a bit of a lonely person, right?”
“Itsuki!”
Before Father could say anything, Itsuki stepped in and provoked him. It felt like Itsuki hit the mark more accurately.
“Come on, give him the cool guy label, at least for a first impression.”
“Naofumi, are you trying to say that I’m actually a lonely guy?”
“Not exactly, but given your age, it’s kind of understandable that you come off that way…”
Father was trying to dodge the subject.
“That’s not the case anymore, right? You’re living a dramatic life in another world now.”
“Ugh… well, yeah.”
As for Itsuki, he seemed to be going along with the flow as if it were just another task. Loose lips sink ships, I say.
“Chuunibyou? If anything, Ren’s more of a power junkie!”
“Ugh… I can’t deny that…!”
“Motoyasu-san, aren’t you more of a romance junkie yourself?”
Well observed. Even in online games, I was always chasing after pigs.
“Itsuki, no matter how close we are, you should learn to sugarcoat things a bit. Is your accuracy skill also working with words?”
At Father’s comment, Itsuki twitched and looked up from the documents. Something seemed to hit the mark, and he gave a wry smile.
“That was a good one.”
“I’m the one who said it, but I wasn’t aiming for it to be that sharp, you know?”
“So, basically, we’re looking for someone who gives off a similar vibe to me?”
“That’s about right. If we think about how Ren would act, we might be able to find him… maybe.”
Father’s words made Ren think deeply.
“If he doesn’t like the country or understands the political situation, he’d probably hide his weapon and pretend to be an adventurer.”

“Yeah, that sounds right. It’s better not to rely too much on the weapon as a clue. Even though the adventurer’s guild has been gathering information on a missing person, nothing’s come up there either.”
“Maybe he’s had plastic surgery or something?”
I’ve heard of that before. Pigs often mess with their bodies just to make themselves look better. But no matter how much they dress it up, if their insides don’t match, they’re still pigs.
Are they trying to turn themselves into meat?
Truly, pigs meant for slaughter!
HAHAHA!
“Or maybe he’s using magic to alter facial recognition? It’d be helpful if we had someone with resistance to illusions.”
Oh? I think the big sister had that kind of ability. Come to think of it, I haven’t met her even once in this loop. …It’s a bit concerning, so I should consult Father about it.
“Then maybe we should ask big sis—”
Just as I was about to say it, a loud voice echoed from the hall of the adventurer’s guild outside the room. It was a deep, manly voice.
“What’s that?”
“Well, it’s the adventurer’s guild. Maybe some ill-mannered adventurers are causing trouble?”
“Maybe… We’ve pretty much gone through the documents, so if it gets out of hand, we should go check it out.”
“Yeah, we should probably head to the next town soon anyway.”
“Agreed.”
“Are we done yet?”
It seemed that Sakura-chan and the others had been having fun throwing the paper airplanes Father had made for them. I wanted to play with them too.
“Alright, everyone, let’s go.”
“Okay!”
“Nano! I want you to make more things that fly, nano!”
“Next time, maybe bamboo dragonflies? Or we could make a model airplane with chopsticks.”
“That sounds fun!”
“Yeah!”
The assistant and the mole started getting excited. Even though we could still hear the loud voice outside, things were surprisingly peaceful here. They must have grown through all these battles.
“Naofumi-san is really good with kids.”
“Yeah.”
“Ren, Itsuki, don’t just sit back and watch. You should play with them too. Sword fights or even musical performances would be fine.”
“I want to play with Naofumi too!”
“…There’s a big kid right here.”
“True.”
“Motoyasu-kun…”
“Iwatani-dono’s struggles… we all understand them. You don’t have to carry everything alone.”
“But it’s everyone making him bear the burden…”
Is it just me, or does it feel like everyone is sympathizing with Father a little too much? And with that, we left the room and headed toward the source of the commotion.
Chapter 681 – Attention

It looks like some adventurers are fighting in the square in front of the Adventurer’s Guild. The spectators include passersby and other adventurers, and in the center of the circle, a fight is currently taking place. One of them looks rough, with a dark complexion, a sturdy build, and a simple-minded vibe—someone who looks like he’d fit in with a bunch of bandits. Is he using his fists as weapons? He’s equipped with knuckles. The other one looks Japanese. Since there are quite a few descendants of people from another world in this world, it’s not surprising to see someone who looks like that. How old would he be? About the same as Ren or Itsuki, I’d say. He still has a bit of youthful innocence left. He’s wearing light armor and seems to be handling his opponent with just a one-handed sword.
“Hey! Quit running around!”
“…Is this all you’ve got?”
The Japanese-looking one seems to be on the offensive. His level is probably higher.
“Buuu!”
It looks like there are about three pigs cheering for the Japanese-looking one. Three of them… how unpleasant. They remind me of someone.
“This is the end!”
The Japanese-looking one knocked away the knuckles with his sword and used the opening to point his sword at his opponent’s neck. Oh, not killing him is quite an admirable attitude.
“The match is over.”
“Damn…”
The brawny adventurer groaned regretfully.
“Bubububu!”
“Bububu!”
The pigs are making a fuss, acting all triumphant. It’s clear that this isn’t a situation that leaves a good impression.
How should I put it… this is triggering my trauma! Specifically, it’s reminding me of the time when I used to chase after pigs and acted the same way with that crimson swine.
“H-Hey, is that really you!?”
The brawny adventurer raised his voice in surprise.
What’s this now? Is that guy famous or something?
“Father, what did that pig say?”
“She was bragging about something. He’s asking if the guy doesn’t know that he’s become a famous adventurer lately.”
“Hmm…”
“Ooooh!”
A cheer went up. Looks like he’s somewhat well-known.
“Bubu!”
“That’s right!”
“Don’t get cocky just because you’re a little strong!”
“Damn…”

It seems that the brawny one was a notorious adventurer who had been getting too full of himself lately. The people around started siding with the Japanese-looking one. The brawny adventurer left in frustration, as if running away.
“Man, that was satisfying!”
“That guy’s been acting all high and mighty lately, so everyone was fed up with him.”
“Well done!”

Hmm… Since we weren’t here from the start, it’s a bit difficult for us to grasp the situation. However, perhaps trying to act cool, the Japanese-looking adventurer scratched his head in annoyance and walked over to the pigs who seemed to be his companions. Then, he handed over the sword he was holding.
“Ah! The Hero’s party!?”

As I clapped my hands along with the others, one of them noticed us behind them and raised his voice, making way for us. Then, the others followed suit, shrinking back and opening a path for us toward the Japanese-looking adventurer.
Why is this happening? We’re not particularly interested in some random adventurer.
“We were just watching…”
“Doesn’t this atmosphere make it feel like we have to go talk to him?”
“Seems like it.”
Father and the others, following the mood, waved as they stepped out of the circle and approached the adventurer.
“You’ve got pretty good skills, don’t you?”

I felt that the Japanese-looking adventurer was giving Ren a suspicious look. Well, it’s not hard to see how Ren’s tone might come off as condescending. This is probably one of the reasons Ren is often misunderstood.
“Ren-san, that attitude is rude right off the bat.”
Itsuki said that to clear up the misunderstanding.

“We are the Four Cardinal Heroes, and we just happened to stop by and see what was going on. I’m the Bow Hero, Kawasumi Itsuki. This is the Sword Hero, Amaki Ren. Over there is the Shield Hero, Iwatani Naofumi, and that one is the Spear Hero—”
“The Love Hunter! Kitamura Motoyasu, at your service!”
A sudden self-introduction. I made sure to emphasize it so there’s no mistake. While my title is the Spear Hero, my profession is the Love Hunter.
The Japanese-looking adventurer glanced around, giving us a once-over before putting on a faint, practiced smile.
“I’m Yuta Railvatz. Nice to meet you.”
“Bubu!”
“Bububu!”
“Bub!”
The three pigs chimed in as well. Leaving the pigs aside, he seems relatively decent.
“Yuta…? A Japanese name?”
“Iwatani-dono, many parents give their children names like those of the heroes. It’s not unusual.”

Éclair explained the situation. I see, so that’s how it is. Come to think of it, Takt also sounds like a Japanese name. That said, because of this, my impression of this Yuta fellow is absolutely the worst.
“Oh, is that so? I guess it’s like being named after a hero or something?”
“Um… so, what do you want with us?”
The adventurer named Yuta asked cautiously. Ren was the one who answered.
“No, as Itsuki just said, we just happened to come across this commotion. That’s all.”
“Yeah, since the others cleared a path for us, ignoring it felt rude.”

Because of Ren and Itsuki’s words, silence fell over the area. The spectators began murmuring. Father looked at us with a troubled expression. However, there’s nothing noteworthy to comment on. The most that can be said is what Ren pointed out —that he has decent skills.

Indeed, for a mere adventurer, his abilities are relatively good, aren’t they? But that’s about it. Simply put, he wouldn’t be able to beat Ren. Whether in skill or anything else. As for Itsuki, he could probably shoot him down from a distance with pinpoint accuracy, and even if I were cornered, I could easily brush him off. Father would probably read his moves and dodge them. If trained, he might reach Éclair’s level, but that’s about it.
“Bububuhi.”
The pig said something.
“Huh? Words of praise? Why? Wasn’t that just a fight?”

Father asked with a genuinely puzzled expression. He tilted his head, looking at me, Ren, and Itsuki for an explanation. But I don’t understand it either. Ren and Itsuki seemed equally confused, unsure how to respond.

To begin with, why should we offer words of praise to someone like him? If being the winner of a fight makes someone great, then I’m the greatest. But that’s not how reality works. It’s those who are intelligent, gentlemanly, and willing to fight for others who deserve praise. I’m striving to become a man worthy of Filo-tan.
“Linelle!”
Yuta, or whatever his name is, stopped the pig.
“Well, we have things to do, so we’ll be going…”
With a business-like smile, Yuta distanced himself from us as if trying to escape. Following his lead, the others around us also began to disperse.
“Did I say something wrong? The woman with him was looking at us like she couldn’t believe what she was seeing…”
“No, I don’t think Naofumi’s reaction was strange.”
“Yes, at least from my perspective, Naofumi-san’s response was the more natural one.”
“I agree with the heroes. I can’t understand what she was thinking when she asked that.”
Same here.
What were those people trying to do?
“By the way, didn’t it remind you of a scene from a sports manga where an upperclassman notices the protagonist and starts paying attention to them?”
“Ah, yes, that’s true. It felt like they were trying to force that upperclassman role onto us, didn’t it?”
“I don’t read much manga, but I thought the same.”

Indeed. There was an air of trying to force us to remember them. Unfortunately, he’s not someone worth that much attention. Perhaps the kind of talent that comes along once every three months. Among the slaves in Father’s domain, there were plenty like him. With that level, I’ll probably forget him by tomorrow.
What was his name again? Cola, was it?
“And that attitude of running away… It’s like saying, ‘I don’t want to stand out, but please remember me,’ right?”
“I feel like if I hadn’t learned the truth from Motoyasu-san, I might have ended up like that.”
“Ah… yeah. Saying you don’t want to stand out while doing things that make you stand out.”
“Yes, how should I put it… he didn’t actually take any action, but it feels like looking at my past self, and it’s stirring up old traumas…”
“What was the cause of the commotion?”
Ren asked a nearby guild staff member.
“Ah, um… It seems that the large adventurer earlier provoked that person at the request counter, and it escalated from a verbal argument into a fight…”
“That’s such a typical scenario. I didn’t think it actually happened in real life.”
Father seemed oddly amused. I suppose he enjoys these cliché scenarios.
“Isn’t it just beating up a disposable character in a predictable position…?”
“And then the women around them started boasting, ‘That’s the famous adventurer Yuta-sama!’ like it was some sort of trump card.”
“A complete textbook scenario.”
“Nano? Is he famous?”
My rival asked. I don’t know. At the very least, across all the loops so far, I have no recollection of anyone named Cola.
